subject: Clarifying remedy & financial cap carve-out for IP infringement (AcmeTech)
messages:
From: Sophie Allen <sophie.allen@acmetech.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@acmetech.com>, Acme Legal <legal@acmetech.com>
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA - order form questions

Hi Logan,

Thanks for sending the MSA redline. We reviewed section 9 (Limitation of Liability). Acme is comfortable with the general cap, but we need a clear carve-out for IP infringement remedies that preserves reasonable remediation and injunctive relief, and we also want the cap to exclude amounts payable under the IP indemnity. Specifically: we expect the liability cap NOT to apply to (i) amounts payable under indemnity for third-party IP claims, and (ii) direct costs reasonably incurred to remediate infringement (including reasonable attorney fees and court-ordered damages).

Can you confirm Redwood is open to: 1) explicit carve-out language for IP indemnities, and 2) a short remediation-cost carve-out for direct remediation expenses up to the same cap? We can discuss escrow or insurance offsets if needed. Attaching Acme's suggested redline excerpt for reference.

Regards,
Sophie Allen
Director, Procurement
AcmeTech

Attachment: AcmeTech_IP_comments_0508.docx (docx)

From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Allen <sophie.allen@acmetech.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 10:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA - order form questions

Sophie — thanks for the clear ask. High level: Redwood is willing to carve IP indemnity amounts out of the monetary cap, but we have a few asks on scope and proof (e.g., notice, control of defense, mitigation). For remediation costs we want to limit vague categories ("reasonable remediation"); we can accept "direct, documented, reasonable" remediation expenses and preserve injunctive relief.

I've looped in legal (Marissa, Elliot) to propose specific language and any necessary fallback (escrow/insurance). Can we schedule a short call Wednesday to run through the proposed text? I'll also share our redline and a short matrix showing what stays inside vs outside the cap.

Best,
Logan Wright
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Redwood_MSA_redline_v3.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 9 May 2028 13:27:00 -07:00
Subject: FW: Redwood MSA - proposed carve-out language

Folks — draft proposed language below for inclusion in section 9. I kept it tight to avoid opening other indemnities: 

--- PROPOSED SNIPPET (draft) ---
For the avoidance of doubt, the Limitation of Liability in this Agreement shall not apply to (a) amounts paid by Redwood pursuant to Section X (Intellectual Property Indemnity) for third-party claims of intellectual property infringement; and (b) direct, documented, and reasonable remediation costs actually incurred by Customer to cure an infringement caused by Redwood Deliverables, provided such costs are no greater than those necessary to restore Customer to the position it occupied prior to the infringement. Nothing in this section shall be deemed to limit either party's right to seek injunctive or equitable relief.
--- END SNIPPET ---

Notes / negotiation positions:
- Keep remediation costs narrowly defined and "documented" to avoid open-ended exposure.
- Insist on Redwood's right to assume defense/control (usual IP indemnity language) and require Customer cooperation.
- If Acme insists on an absolute carve-out for remediation costs without documentation, propose escrow or a capped remediation line item instead.

If agreeable, Logan can send to Sophie with a short explanation and a 30-minute slot proposal.

Marissa Cole
Sr. Counsel, Redwood Inference

Attachment: Escrow_Terms_Summary.pdf (pdf)

From: Sophie Allen <sophie.allen@acmetech.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Hsu <tom.hsu@acmetech.com>, Acme Legal <legal@acmetech.com>
Date: Wed, 10 May 2028 09:48:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Redwood MSA - proposed carve-out language

Thanks Marissa and Logan — that draft is close to what we had in mind. A couple of clarifications from Acme Legal:
1) We want the remediation-cost carve-out to explicitly include reasonable outside counsel fees and court-ordered damages (not punitive).
2) We will accept Redwood's right to assume defense provided Redwood remains liable for direct remediation costs if the adjudicated remedy requires remediation beyond what defense achieves.

Acme prefers language that is explicit rather than relying on "for the avoidance of doubt" phrasing. I've attached a short markup showing the two additions. We remain open to a capped escrow if Redwood prefers a fixed budget approach for remediation.

Sophie
Director, Procurement, AcmeTech

Attachment: AcmeTech_IP_comments_0508.docx (docx)

From: Elliot Price <elliot.price@redwood.com>
To: Sophie Allen <sophie.allen@acmetech.com>, Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel.kim@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 11 May 2028 16:02:00 -07:00
Subject: RE: Redwood MSA - final proposal and next steps

Sophie/Team — appreciate the quick turnaround. Based on Acme's notes, Redwood will accept the following compromise to be incorporated into the Order Form (clean language to follow):

1) Monetary cap does not apply to amounts Redwood pays under Redwood's IP indemnity obligations for third-party infringement claims (typical carve-out).
2) Monetary cap does not apply to direct remediation costs reasonably and actually incurred by Customer to cure an infringement caused by Redwood, including reasonable outside counsel fees and court-ordered damages (excluding punitive, exemplary, or consequential damages). Customer must provide documentation and give Redwood the opportunity to cure; Redwood may assume defense/control.
3) If the parties cannot agree on remediation costs in good faith, either party can trigger escalation to the dispute resolution path in Section 14; as an interim measure, teams may agree to place disputed remediation funds in escrow pending resolution.

Logan will share the clean redline and the DocuSign order form link once we have Acme's confirmation on the above. If that's acceptable, please confirm by end of day Friday and we'll target DocuSign the week of May 15.

Thanks,
Elliot Price
Counsel, Redwood Inference
